title: 2 Kings Bible Quiz - Chapter 18
description: Ten questions on 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah's faithful reign, the fall of Samaria and Rabshakeh's speech at the walls of Jerusalem.

questions.text: What was the name of Hezekiah's mother?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah's mother's name was Abi the daughter of Zechariah.

questions.text: What did Hezekiah call the bronze serpent that Moses had made, which he broke in pieces?
questions.explanation: He broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made, because the children of Israel burned incense to it, and he called it Nehushtan.

questions.text: As far as which city did Hezekiah strike the Philistines?
questions.explanation: He struck the Philistines to Gaza and its borders, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.

questions.text: Which king of Assyria came up against Samaria in the fourth year of King Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.

questions.text: To which city did Hezekiah send to the king of Assyria, saying, "I have offended you"?
questions.explanation: Hezekiah sent to the king of Assyria to Lachish, saying, "I have offended you. Return from me."

questions.text: Where did Tartan, Rabsaris and Rabshakeh stand when they came to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: They came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the fuller's field.

answers.text: By the conduit of the upper pool
In the court of Yahweh's house

questions.text: What did Rabshakeh call Egypt, on which Hezekiah was trusting?
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh said, "You trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt."

answers.text: A wall of bronze and iron
The staff of this bruised reed

questions.text: What did Rabshakeh offer to give if Judah could set riders on them?
questions.explanation: Rabshakeh said, "I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders on them."

questions.text: In which language did Eliakim, Shebnah and Joah ask Rabshakeh to speak?
questions.explanation: They asked him to speak in the Syrian language, and not in the Jews' language in the hearing of the people on the wall.

questions.text: Why did the people on the wall answer Rabshakeh not a word?
questions.explanation: The people stayed quiet, for the king's commandment was, "Don't answer him."

answers.text: They did not understand his language
Isaiah had told them to pray instead
They had already fled the city
The king had commanded, "Don't answer him."
